claim: Arabidopsis thaliana seeds were stratified for three days at 4°C.
source: Seeds of Arabidopsis thaliana (Columbia) sown on agar plates were stratified for three days at 4°C and then transferred to 22°C in the dark.
evidence: The experimental procedure is described in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A showing the experimental design timeline.

claim: After stratification, etiolated seedlings were exposed to continuous white light at 40 µmol/m2/s.
source: After 3 days, etiolated seedlings were exposed to continuous white light (40 µmol/m2/s) and harvested at different time points during de-etiolation.
evidence: The experimental conditions are stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Chlorophyll levels in whole seedlings increased within the first 4 hr of illumination (T4).
source: Chlorophyll levels in whole seedlings increased within the first 4 hr of illumination (T4) and continued to increase linearly during subsequent illumination as the seedlings grew (Figure 1C).
evidence: Chlorophyll quantification data are presented in Figure 1C showing measurements at different time points.

claim: The maximum quantum yield of PSII (Fv/Fm) reached near maximal value of 0.8 at 14 hr of light exposure (T14).
source: PSII maximum quantum yield increased during the initial period of illumination and was near the maximal value of 0.8 at 14 hr of light exposure (T14), independent of light intensity (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Photosynthetic efficiency measurements are shown in Figure 1D with error bars indicating SD (n = 4–10).

claim: The assembly of a fully functional photosynthetic machinery occurs within the first 14 hr of de-etiolation.
source: Other photosynthetic parameters (photochemical quenching, qP and PSII quantum yield in the light, ΦPSII, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C) reached maximum values at T14 and remained stable thereafter, indicating that the assembly of a fully functional photosynthetic machinery occurs within the first 14 hr of de-etiolation, and that further biosynthesis of photosynthesis related compounds is efficiently coordinated.
evidence: Multiple photosynthetic parameters were measured and shown to reach maximum values at T14 in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Plastids in cotyledons of etiolated seedlings displayed typical etioplast ultrastructure with a paracrystalline PLB and tubular PTs.
source: Plastids present in cotyledons of etiolated seedlings displayed the typical etioplast ultrastructure with a paracrystalline PLB and tubular PTs (Figure 2A).
evidence: TEM images in Figure 2A show the etioplast structure at T0.

claim: The observed PLBs were constituted of hexagonal units with diameters of 0.8–1 µm.
source: The observed PLBs were constituted of hexagonal units with diameters of 0.8–1 µm (Figure 2E).
evidence: Measurements of PLB structure are reported in the text and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: By T4, the highly structured PLBs progressively disappeared and thylakoid lamellae were formed.
source: By T4, the highly structured PLBs progressively disappeared and thylakoid lamellae were formed (Figure 2B).
evidence: TEM images in Figure 2B show the transition from PLB to thylakoid lamellae at T4.

claim: The lamellae at T4 were blurry and their thickness varied between 15 and 70 nm.
source: The lamellae were blurry and their thickness varied between 15 and 70 nm (Figure 2F).
evidence: Lamellae thickness measurements are reported in the text and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: After 24 hr of illumination (T24), appressed regions corresponding to developing grana stacks appeared.
source: After 24 hr of illumination (T24), the density of lamellae per chloroplast was higher than that at T4 due to an increase in lamellar length and number. Appressed regions corresponding to developing grana stacks also appeared by T24 (Figure 2C and G).
evidence: TEM images in Figure 2C and G show the appearance of grana stacks at T24.

claim: Early grana stacks at T24 consisted of 2–6 lamellae with a thickness of 13 nm each.
source: These early grana stacks consisted of 2–6 lamellae with a thickness of 13 nm each (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Measurements of grana stack structure are reported in the text and detailed in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Starch granules were present at T24, supporting that these chloroplasts are photosynthetically functional and able to assimilate carbon dioxide (CO2).
source: In addition, starch granules were present at T24, supporting the notion that these chloroplasts are photosynthetically functional and able to assimilate carbon dioxide (CO2).
evidence: The presence of starch granules is observed in TEM images and interpreted as evidence of photosynthetic function.

claim: At T96, grana stacks consisted of up to 10 lamellae per grana.
source: At T96, thylakoid membrane organization was visually similar to that at T24, but with more layers per grana (up to 10 lamellae per grana; Figure 2D and H).
evidence: TEM images in Figure 2D and H show increased grana stacking at T96.

claim: Singular lamella thickness at T96 increased by 2–3 nm compared to that at T24.
source: In addition, singular lamella thickness at T96 increased by 2–3 nm compared to that at T24 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Lamella thickness measurements are detailed in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Etioplast average length was 2 µm (±0.9, n = 10) in the dark (T0).
source: Etioplast average length (estimated by measuring the maximum distance on individual slices) was 2 µm (±0.9, n = 10) in the dark (T0), whereas chloroplast average length was 6 µm (±1.62, n = 10) at T96 (Table 1).
evidence: Plastid length measurements are reported in Table 1.

claim: Chloroplast average length was 6 µm (±1.62, n = 10) at T96.
source: Etioplast average length (estimated by measuring the maximum distance on individual slices) was 2 µm (±0.9, n = 10) in the dark (T0), whereas chloroplast average length was 6 µm (±1.62, n = 10) at T96 (Table 1).
evidence: Plastid length measurements are reported in Table 1.

claim: Photosynthetically functional thylakoid membranes form rapidly during the first 24 hr of de-etiolation.
source: Collectively, these data show that photosynthetically functional thylakoid membranes form rapidly during the first 24 hr of de-etiolation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined ultrastructural and photosynthetic data presented.

claim: The total chloroplast volume increased about 11-fold from T4 (9.4 µm3) to T96 (112.14 µm3).
source: The total chloroplast volume increased about 11-fold from T4 (9.4 µm3) to T96 (112.14 µm3) (Table 1).
evidence: Chloroplast volume measurements from SBF-SEM analysis are reported in Table 1.

claim: The thylakoid surface area increased about 30-fold reaching 2086 (±393) µm2 per chloroplast at T96.
source: In parallel, the thylakoid surface area (stroma side) increased about 30-fold reaching 2086 (±393) µm2 per chloroplast at T96 (Figure 4A and Table 1).
evidence: Thylakoid surface area measurements from SBF-SEM analysis are shown in Figure 4A and Table 1.

claim: The surface area increased drastically between T4 and T24 (about 22-fold) and much less (about 1.4-fold) between T24 and T96.
source: The surface area increased drastically between T4 and T24 (about 22-fold) and much less (about 1.4-fold) between T24 and T96.
evidence: This is calculated from the thylakoid surface area data presented in Figure 4A and Table 1.

claim: The ratio of the thylakoid to envelope surface area increased drastically from T4 to T24, but decreased slightly between T24 and T96.
source: Accordingly, quantification of the envelope surface area indicated that the ratio of the thylakoid to envelope surface area increased drastically from T4 to T24, but decreased slightly between T24 and T96 (Table 1).
evidence: The thylakoid/envelope surface ratio is calculated and reported in Table 1.

claim: More than 5000 proteins were robustly identified and quantified by label-free shot-gun mass spectrometry.
source: Quantification was restricted to protein (groups) with at least two identified peptides among which at least one is unique to the protein (group). Using these requirements, 5082 Arabidopsis proteins (or groups) were identified.
evidence: The number of identified proteins is stated based on the proteomics analysis criteria.

claim: The first 12 hr of illumination (T12) saw very few statistically significant changes in protein abundance.
source: Based on this proteomic approach, the first 12 hr of illumination (T12) saw very few statistically significant changes in protein abundance (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Proteomic data analysis shows minimal changes in protein abundance during early de-etiolation.

claim: Significant changes in protein abundance were observed only after 8 hr of illumination when considering a q-value <0.01 as a stringent threshold value.
source: Considering a q-value <0.01 as a stringent threshold value, significant changes were observed only after 8 hr of illumination.
evidence: Statistical analysis of proteomic data with specified threshold values.

claim: At 8 hr, the abundance of cryptochrome 2 decreased and the abundance of three proteins (PsbS, Lhcb5, Lhcb6) belonging to chlorophyll a/b binding proteins increased.
source: These changes correspond to the decreased abundance of only one protein (the photoreceptor cryptochrome 2, consistent with its photolabile property) and increased levels of only three proteins, which belonged to the chlorophyll a/b binding proteins category involved in photoprotection (AT1G44575 = PsbS; AT4G10340 = Lhcb5; AT1G15820 = Lhcb6; Chen et al., 2018; Li et al., 2000).
evidence: Specific protein changes at 8 hr are identified from proteomic data and supported by literature citations.

claim: A drastic change of proteome composition occurred by T24, with 402 proteins showing a significant increase in abundance with over twofold change (FC >2; q-value <0.01) compared with the etiolated stage.
source: A drastic change of proteome composition occurred by T24, with 402 proteins showing a significant increase in abundance with over twofold change (FC >2; q-value <0.01) compared with the etiolated stage, and 107 proteins showing a significant decrease with over twofold change (FC <0.5; q-value <0.01).
evidence: Statistical analysis of proteomic data at T24 shows significant proteome changes.

claim: The 100 most-upregulated proteins at T24 comprised proteins related to photosynthesis, proteins constituting the core and antennae of photosystems, and proteins involved in carbon fixation.
source: As expected, the 100 most-upregulated proteins comprised proteins related to photosynthesis, proteins constituting the core and antennae of photosystems, and proteins involved in carbon fixation (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Analysis of the most upregulated proteins from proteomic data.

claim: 1112 proteins were assigned to plastids based on SUBA4 localization consensus.
source: According to the SUBA4 localization consensus, 1112 proteins were assigned to plastids, which covers about a third of the total plastid proteome (Ferro et al., 2003; Hooper et al., 2017; Kleffmann et al., 2007).
evidence: Protein localization assignment is based on the SUBA4 database and supported by literature citations.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of plastid-localized proteins revealed six main clusters with different accumulation patterns.
source: Generation of a global heatmap for each of the 1112 potential plastidial proteins revealed different accumulation patterns (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1—source data 1). Hierarchical clustering showed a categorization into six main clusters.
evidence: Hierarchical clustering analysis of proteomic data is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cluster 1 contained proteins whose relative amounts decreased during de-etiolation.
source: Cluster 1 (purple) contained proteins whose relative amounts decreased during de-etiolation.
evidence: Cluster characteristics are described based on hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Clusters 2 and 6 displayed the largest amplitude of differential accumulation and were enriched in proteins related to the light reactions of photosynthesis.
source: Proteins in clusters 2 and 6 displayed the largest amplitude of differential accumulation. Gene ontology (GO) analysis (Mi et al., 2019) indicated a statistically significant overrepresentation of proteins related to the light reactions of photosynthesis in clusters 2 and 6 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: GO analysis of protein clusters is performed and results are reported with citation to the analysis method.

claim: All photosynthesis-related proteins increased in abundance during de-etiolation.
source: In agreement with that depicted in the global heatmap (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), all photosynthesis-related proteins increased in abundance during de-etiolation (Figure 5A).
evidence: Photosynthesis-related protein accumulation patterns are shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Among eight detected chloroplast-localized proteins related to lipid biosynthesis, FAB1 and FAD7 levels increased only between T72 and T96.
source: Among the eight detected proteins, two appeared differentially regulated; fatty acid binding protein 1 (FAB1) and fatty acid desaturase 7 (FAD7) levels increased only between 72 hr of illumination (T72) and T96, whereas the other proteins gradually accumulated over the course of de-etiolation (Figure 5B).
evidence: Lipid biosynthesis protein accumulation patterns are shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Illumination resulted in increased amounts of most proteins of the chlorophyll biosynthesis pathway, except PORA and to a lesser extent PORB, which decreased.
source: In agreement, illumination resulted in increased amounts of most of all detected proteins of the chlorophyll biosynthesis pathway, except PORA and to a lesser extent PORB, which clearly decreased and were separated from other chlorophyll-related proteins (Figure 5C and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Chlorophyll biosynthesis protein accumulation patterns are shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The TOC receptors TOC120 and TOC132 were more abundant in etioplasts compared to fully-developed chloroplasts.
source: Accordingly, the TOC receptors TOC120 and TOC132, which are important for the import of proteins in non-photosynthetic tissues, were more abundant in etioplasts compared to fully-developed chloroplasts (compare T0 and T96).
evidence: Comparison of TOC receptor abundance between T0 and T96 from proteomic data.

claim: The general import channel TOC75 (TOC75 III) maintained stable expression levels throughout de-etiolation.
source: The general import channel TOC75 (TOC75 III) maintained stable expression levels throughout de-etiolation, reflecting its general role in protein import.
evidence: TOC75 protein levels from proteomic data show stability across time points.

claim: Immunoblot analysis revealed that the abundance of phyA dropped during the first 4 hr of light exposure.
source: However, immunoblots revealed that the abundance of phyA dropped already during the first 4 hr of light exposure (Figure 6), as previously reported (e.g. Debrieux and Fankhauser, 2010).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6 show phyA decrease at early time points, supported by literature citation.

claim: HY5 showed transient accumulation between 4 and 72 hr by immunoblot.
source: The increase of HY5 peptide abundance was not significant by proteomics but we observed a transient accumulation of the protein between 4 and 72 hr by immunoblot (Figure 5—source data 1; Figure 6) consistent with the previously reported regulation of abundance during seedling development (Hardtke et al., 2000).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6 show HY5 accumulation pattern, supported by literature citation.

claim: PsbA and PsbD proteins were detectable in seedlings at T4, gradually increasing thereafter.
source: PsbA and PsbD (PSII reaction center core), PsbO (Oxygen Evolving Complex), and Lhcb2 (outer antenna complex) proteins were detectable in seedlings at T4, gradually increasing thereafter.
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show detection and accumulation of these proteins.

claim: Accumulation of the PSI proteins PsaC and PsaD and the Cyt b6f complex protein PetC started at T8.
source: Accumulation of the PSI proteins PsaC and PsaD and the Cyt b6f complex protein PetC started later; these proteins were detectable starting at T8 (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show detection of these proteins starting at T8.

claim: AtpC (ATP synthase complex) was detectable in the etioplast.
source: Interestingly, AtpC (ATP synthase complex) was detectable in the etioplast, as described previously (Plöscher et al., 2011).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show AtpC detection at T0, supported by literature citation.

claim: ELIPs (Early Light Induced Protein) transiently accumulated upon the dark-to-light transition.
source: As expected, ELIPs (Early Light Induced Protein) transiently accumulated upon the dark-to-light transition (Figure 6A; Kimura et al., 2003).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show ELIP accumulation pattern, supported by literature citation.

claim: PORA accumulated in etiolated seedlings (T0) and then progressively disappeared upon light exposure.
source: As in the proteome analysis, PORA accumulated in etiolated seedlings (T0) and then progressively disappeared upon light exposure.
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6A show PORA accumulation and decrease pattern.

claim: PsbA levels were about twice that of PsaC at T96.
source: In addition, the comparison of PsbA and PsaC (representative proteins of PSII and PSI, respectively) showed that PsbA levels were about twice that of PsaC at T96 (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: Quantitative immunoblot data in Figure 6B and C show the relative abundance of PsbA and PsaC.

claim: MGDG 18:3/16:3, MGDG 18:3/18:3, MGDG 18:3/16:1, DGDG 18:3/18:3, and DGDG 18:3/16:0 were the most abundant lipids detected at all time points.
source: MGDG 18:3/16:3, MGDG 18:3/18:3, MGDG 18:3/16:1, DGDG 18:3/18:3, and DGDG 18:3/16:0 were the most abundant lipids detected at all time points.
evidence: Lipidomic analysis identified and quantified these galactolipid species.

claim: Clustering analysis identified two distinct kinetic patterns of galactolipid accumulation corresponding to the ER and PL pathways.
source: Accumulation of all galactolipids increased upon de-etiolation; however, clustering analysis identified two distinct kinetic patterns. One group displayed a leap between T8 and T12, whereas the other group increased later during the de-etiolation period (Figure 7C). Interestingly, the two clusters separated the lipids according to the two pathways described for galactolipid synthesis, namely the ER and PL pathways (Figure 7A and B; Marechal et al., 1997; Ohlrogge and Browse, 1995).
evidence: Clustering analysis of lipidomic data shown in Figure 7 reveals pathway-specific accumulation patterns, supported by literature citations.

claim: During early stages of de-etiolation (T0–T24), there was incremental accumulation of MGDG and DGDG galactolipids derived from the ER pathway.
source: During early stages of de-etiolation (T0–T24), we observed an incremental accumulation of MGDG and DGDG galactolipids derived from the ER pathway, whereas galactolipids from the PL pathway started to accumulate at T24 (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: Lipidomic data in Figure 7A and B show pathway-specific accumulation patterns.

claim: Galactolipids from the PL pathway started to accumulate at T24.
source: During early stages of de-etiolation (T0–T24), we observed an incremental accumulation of MGDG and DGDG galactolipids derived from the ER pathway, whereas galactolipids from the PL pathway started to accumulate at T24 (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: Lipidomic data in Figure 7A and B show PL pathway galactolipids accumulating starting at T24.

claim: The MGDG/DGDG ratio decreased between T0 and T8, which was associated with the transition from PLB to thylakoid membrane.
source: The MGDG/DGDG ratio decreased between T0 and T8. This was associated with the transition from PLB (cubic lipid phase) to thylakoid membrane (lamellar structure) (Bottier et al., 2007).
evidence: MGDG/DGDG ratio calculation from lipidomic data in Figure 7D, with interpretation supported by literature citation.

claim: The MGDG/DGDG ratio started to increase gradually at T8 and was constant by T72 and T96.
source: The MGDG/DGDG ratio started to increase gradually at T8 and was constant by T72 and T96 (Figure 7D).
evidence: MGDG/DGDG ratio data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The chloroplast number per cell was constant from T4 (25 ± 8) to T24 (26 ± 6).
source: The chloroplast number per cell was constant from T4 (25 ± 8) to T24 (26 ± 6); however, in parallel with cell expansion (Figure 8A and B), chloroplast number increased sharply (fourfold increase) between T24 (26 ± 6) and T96 (112 ± 29), indicating that two rounds of chloroplast division occurred during this time.
evidence: Chloroplast number per cell was quantified from SBF-SEM data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Chloroplast number increased sharply (fourfold increase) between T24 (26 ± 6) and T96 (112 ± 29), indicating that two rounds of chloroplast division occurred during this time.
source: The chloroplast number per cell was constant from T4 (25 ± 8) to T24 (26 ± 6); however, in parallel with cell expansion (Figure 8A and B), chloroplast number increased sharply (fourfold increase) between T24 (26 ± 6) and T96 (112 ± 29), indicating that two rounds of chloroplast division occurred during this time.
evidence: Chloroplast number quantification from SBF-SEM data in Figure 8A, with inference about division rounds.

claim: FtsZ1, FtsZ2-1, and FtsZ2-2 proteins were detectable during early time points of de-etiolation and accumulated significantly between T24 and T48.
source: Immunoblot analysis of FILAMENTOUS TEMPERATURE-SENSITIVE FtsZ1, FtsZ2-1, and FtsZ2-2 proteins showed that these key components of the chloroplast division machinery were already present during the early time points of de-etiolation. We observed considerably increased accumulation of these proteins between T24 and T48, consistent with the idea that activation of chloroplast division takes place at T24, leading the proliferation of chloroplasts (Figure 8C).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8C show FtsZ protein accumulation patterns.

claim: ARC5 protein levels clearly increased during de-etiolation between T8 and T12.
source: However, levels of ACCUMULATION AND REPLICATION OF CHLOROPLAST 5 (ARC5) protein, another key component of the chloroplast division machinery, clearly increased during de-etiolation between T8 and T12, presumably reflecting assembly of the chloroplast division machinery before its activation and the proliferation of chloroplasts (Figure 8D).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8D show ARC5 protein accumulation pattern.

claim: The average volume of dividing chloroplasts at T24 and T96 were consistently higher than the average volume of all chloroplasts.
source: The average volume of dividing chloroplasts at T24 and T96 were consistently higher than the average volume of all chloroplasts (96 µm3 and 136 µm3 compared to 62 µm3 and 112 µm3, respectively) (Figure 4B, Figure 8E and Figure 8—source data 1) indicating that smaller chloroplasts are not dividing.
evidence: Volume measurements of dividing chloroplasts from SBF-SEM data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Developing chloroplasts only divide once a certain chloroplast volume is reached.
source: This indicates that developing chloroplasts only divide once a certain chloroplast volume is reached.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that dividing chloroplasts have larger volumes than average.

claim: The total thylakoid surface area present in seedling cotyledons at T96 was about 700 mm2.
source: By T96, the latest time point of our analysis, the total surface area of thylakoids present in the seedling cotyledons was about 700 mm2 (see values in Table 1 for calculation), about 500-fold greater than the surface area of one cotyledon at this developmental stage.
evidence: Calculation based on data in Table 1.

claim: The total thylakoid surface area at T96 was about 500-fold greater than the surface area of one cotyledon at this developmental stage.
source: By T96, the latest time point of our analysis, the total surface area of thylakoids present in the seedling cotyledons was about 700 mm2 (see values in Table 1 for calculation), about 500-fold greater than the surface area of one cotyledon at this developmental stage.
evidence: Comparison calculation based on thylakoid and cotyledon surface area data.

claim: The reorganization of pre-existing molecules rather than de novo synthesis is responsible for the major chloroplast ultrastructural changes that occur between T0 and T4.
source: Therefore, our data suggest that the reorganization of pre-existing molecules rather than de novo synthesis is responsible for the major chloroplast ultrastructural changes that occur between T0 and T4.
evidence: This interpretation is based on the observation of minimal protein and lipid changes between T0 and T4 despite major ultrastructural changes.

claim: These results are consistent with other studies reporting only minor increases in protein accumulation and translation during initial chloroplast differentiation.
source: These results are consistent with other studies reporting only minor increases in protein accumulation and translation during initial chloroplast differentiation (Dubreuil et al., 2018; Kleffmann et al., 2007; Reiland et al., 2011).
evidence: Comparison with literature findings supports the observation.

claim: At T96 the abundance of 607 proteins (12% of the identified) was increased.
source: At T96 the abundance of 607 proteins (12% of the identified) was increased which confirm the massive reorganization of the proteome following the reorganization of the transcriptome during photomorphogenesis (Ma et al., 2001).
evidence: Proteomic data analysis at T96 with comparison to transcriptome studies cited.

claim: Most photosynthesis-related proteins are globally coregulated.
source: GO analysis combined with expression pattern–based hierarchical clustering highlighted that most photosynthesis-related proteins are globally coregulated (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, clusters 2 and 6) which correlates as well with the overall increase of their corresponding transcripts upon light exposure (Ma et al., 2001).
evidence: GO analysis and clustering of proteomic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1, with comparison to transcriptome studies cited.

claim: PSI subunits were detected at later time points than PSII subunits, but thereafter PSI subunit accumulation was faster.
source: However, targeted immunoblot analysis revealed different accumulation dynamics for specific photosystem subunits: PSI subunits were detected at later time points than PSII subunits, but thereafter PSI subunit accumulation was faster (Figure 6).
evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6 show differential accumulation dynamics of PSI and PSII subunits.

claim: The kinetics of different photosynthetic parameters were consistent with the sequential activation of PSII and PSI.
source: The kinetics of different photosynthetic parameters were consistent with the sequential activation of PSII and PSI, in particular photochemical quenching, which showed increased oxidation of the plastoquinone pool by T14 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Photosynthetic parameter measurements in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 support sequential activation.

claim: Early accumulation of proteins such as Lhcb5, −6, and PSBS could be a way to quickly induce photoprotective mechanisms such as non-photochemical quenching to prevent PSII photodamage during initial photosynthetic machinery assembly.
source: Early accumulation of proteins such as Lhcb5, −6, and PSBS could be a way to quickly induce photoprotective mechanisms such as non-photochemical quenching to prevent PSII photodamage during initial photosynthetic machinery assembly.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed early accumulation of these proteins and their known photoprotective functions.

claim: Differences in PSI and PSII accumulation dynamics and activity have been consistently observed in other chloroplast development experimental systems.
source: Differences in PSI and PSII accumulation dynamics and activity have been consistently observed in other chloroplast development experimental systems, including in Arabidopsis cell cultures, during germination and development of Arabidopsis seedlings in the light, and in tobacco leaves upon reillumination after dark adaptation (Armarego-Marriott et al., 2019; Dubreuil et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2018).
evidence: Comparison with multiple literature studies supports the observation.

claim: The timing of PSII/PSI relative abundance do not match with their preferential localization in specific thylakoid membrane domains.
source: Preferential localization of the PSI and PSII protein complexes in specific thylakoid membrane domains have been reported (lamellae and grana, respectively) (Wietrzynski et al., 2020). Therefore, the timing of PSII/PSI relative abundance do not match with their preferential localization.
evidence: Comparison of observed accumulation timing with known localization patterns from literature.

claim: Galactolipids constitute the bulk of the thylakoid membranes, but are mostly absent from other membrane systems under growth conditions where phosphorus nutrient is available.
source: Galactolipids constitute the bulk of the thylakoid membranes, but are mostly absent from other membrane systems under growth conditions where phosphorus nutrient is available (Jouhet et al., 2007).
evidence: Statement about galactolipid distribution supported by literature citation.

claim: MGDG and DGDG represent around 80% of the thylakoid membrane lipids.
source: MGDG and DGDG represent around 80% of the thylakoid membrane lipids.
evidence: Statement about galactolipid composition of thylakoid membranes.

claim: ER-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the etioplast whereas PL-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the chloroplast.
source: This illustrates the different galactolipid compositions of etioplasts and chloroplasts: ER-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the etioplast whereas PL-pathway galactolipids are predominant in the chloroplast.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the differential accumulation patterns of ER and PL pathway galactolipids.

claim: The emergence of PTs relies on the existing lipids in the etioplast PLB.
source: As no significant changes in lipid accumulation were observed by T4, it appears likely that the emergence of PTs relies on the existing lipids in the etioplast PLB, as suggested also by Armarego-Marriott et al., 2019.
evidence: This interpretation is based on the lack of lipid changes at T4 and supported by literature citation.

claim: Chloroplast development continued between T24 and T96, during which thylakoid membranes acquired grana stacks with more clearly defined organization.
source: Chloroplast development continued between T24 and T96, during which thylakoid membranes acquired grana stacks with more clearly defined organization (Figure 2).
evidence: TEM images in Figure 2 show continued structural development between T24 and T96.

claim: Thylakoid surface increased by only 41% between T24 and T96.
source: Thylakoid surface increased by only 41%; however, chloroplasts continued to enlarge at a rate comparable to previous de-etiolation stages (T0–T24).
evidence: Calculation from thylakoid surface area data.

claim: Chloroplast volume expansion between T24 and T96 may be caused by enlargement of extra-thylakoidal spaces occupied by emerging starch granules.
source: This chloroplast volume expansion may be caused by enlargement of extra-thylakoidal spaces occupied by emerging starch granules.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation of increased starch granules and chloroplast volume without proportional thylakoid surface increase.

claim: Increases in lipids and proteins between T24 and T96 enable the expansion of already functional thylakoid membranes in preparation for chloroplast division.
source: These results suggest that large amounts of lipids and proteins are necessary to build up the thylakoid membrane until T24, whereas increases in lipids and proteins between T24 and T96 enable the expansion of already functional thylakoid membranes in preparation for chloroplast division.
evidence: This interpretation is based on the observed patterns of lipid/protein accumulation and chloroplast division.

claim: Cell number was constant during cotyledon development and was estimated as 3000 mesophyll and palisade cells per seedling at T24 and T96.
source: As reported previously (Pyke and Leech, 1994), cell number was constant during cotyledon development. We estimated this number as 3000 mesophyll and palisade cells per seedling at T24 and T96 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Cell number estimation based on volume calculations shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2, with support from literature citation.

claim: The two approaches (mathematical model and morphometric measurements) showed very similar total thylakoid surface area per seedling at T4 and T24.
source: As shown in Figure 9, the two approaches showed very similar total thylakoid surface area per seedling at T4 and T24 and differences in this parameter by T96.
evidence: Comparison of model predictions with morphometric data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The plateau phase suggested by the model is not validated and other components not included in the model probably contributed to the expansion of thylakoids at later time points of de-etiolation.
source: This indicates that the plateau phase suggested by the model is not validated and that other components that were not included in the model probably contributed to the expansion of thylakoids at later time points of de-etiolation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the discrepancy between model predictions and morphometric data at T96.

claim: De-etiolation is divided into two phases: a 'Structure Establishment Phase' followed by a 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase'.
source: When considering chloroplast development, our study shows that de-etiolation is divided into two phases. We documented structural changes (disassembly of the PLB and the gradual formation of thylakoid lamellae) and initial increases of ER- and PL-pathway galactolipids and photosynthesis-related proteins (PSII, PSI, and Cyt b6f) during the 'Structure Establishment Phase', which was followed by increased chloroplast number in parallel with cell expansion in the 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase'.
evidence: This is a synthesis of the findings from structural, proteomic, and lipidomic analyses.

claim: Compounds used to generate the mathematical model appear to contribute most to changes in thylakoid surface during early stages of de-etiolation (the structure establishment phase).
source: This means that compounds used to generate the mathematical model appear to contribute most to changes in thylakoid surface during early stages of de-etiolation (the structure establishment phase).
evidence: This interpretation is based on the good fit of the model to morphometric data at early time points.

claim: During the later stages of de-etiolation (the chloroplast proliferation phase), the contribution of other compounds omitted in the model is required to build up thylakoid surface.
source: By contrast, during the later stages of de-etiolation (the chloroplast proliferation phase), the contribution of other compounds omitted in our model is obviously required to build up thylakoid surface.
evidence: This interpretation is based on the poor fit of the model to morphometric data at later time points.

claim: FtsH proteases have a critical function during thylakoid biogenesis.
source: Our proteomics data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Dataset 2) revealed some proteins that increased between T24 and T96, such as the FtsH protease (AT2G30950). FtsH proteases have a critical function during thylakoid biogenesis.
evidence: Statement about FtsH function based on proteomic data and general knowledge.

claim: In Arabidopsis, FtsH proteases constitute a hetero-hexameric complex of four FtsH subunits, which is integrated in the thylakoid membrane.
source: In Arabidopsis, they constitute a hetero-hexameric complex of four FtsH subunits, which is integrated in the thylakoid membrane (Kato and Sakamoto, 2018).
evidence: Statement about FtsH complex structure supported by literature citation.

claim: Light triggers chloroplast differentiation whereby the etioplast transforms into a photosynthesizing chloroplast and the thylakoid rapidly emerges.
source: Light triggers chloroplast differentiation whereby the etioplast transforms into a photosynthesizing chloroplast and the thylakoid rapidly emerges.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of the study's focus.

claim: Using Serial Block Face Scanning Electron Microscopy (SBF-SEM), a series of chloroplast 3D reconstructions during differentiation were generated, revealing chloroplast number and volume and the extent of envelope and thylakoid membrane surfaces.
source: Using Serial Block Face Scanning Electron Microscopy (SBF-SEM), we generated a series of chloroplast 3D reconstructions during differentiation, revealing chloroplast number and volume and the extent of envelope and thylakoid membrane surfaces.
evidence: This describes the methodology and results of the SBF-SEM analysis.

claim: Quantitative lipid and whole proteome data were used to complement the (ultra)structural data, providing a time-resolved, multi-dimensional description of chloroplast differentiation.
source: Furthermore, we used quantitative lipid and whole proteome data to complement the (ultra)structural data, providing a time-resolved, multi-dimensional description of chloroplast differentiation.
evidence: This describes the integrated approach of the study.

claim: This study showed two distinct phases of chloroplast biogenesis: an initial photosynthesis-enabling 'Structure Establishment Phase' followed by a 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase' during cell expansion.
source: This showed two distinct phases of chloroplast biogenesis: an initial photosynthesis-enabling 'Structure Establishment Phase' followed by a 'Chloroplast Proliferation Phase' during cell expansion.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The data detail thylakoid membrane expansion during de-etiolation at the seedling level and the relative contribution and differential regulation of proteins and lipids at each developmental stage.
source: Moreover, these data detail thylakoid membrane expansion during de-etiolation at the seedling level and the relative contribution and differential regulation of proteins and lipids at each developmental stage.
evidence: This summarizes the comprehensive nature of the data collected.

claim: A roadmap for chloroplast differentiation, a critical process for plant photoautotrophic growth and survival, was established.
source: Altogether, we establish a roadmap for chloroplast differentiation, a critical process for plant photoautotrophic growth and survival.
evidence: This states the overall contribution of the study.

claim: Light is a crucial factor for chloroplast differentiation.
source: Light is a crucial factor for chloroplast differentiation.
evidence: This is a well-established fact stated in the introduction.

claim: For seeds that germinate in the light, chloroplasts may differentiate directly from proplastids present in cotyledons.
source: For seeds that germinate in the light, chloroplasts may differentiate directly from proplastids present in cotyledons.
evidence: This describes an alternative developmental pathway.

claim: Seeds most often germinate underneath soil, and seedling development typically begins in darkness and follows a skotomorphogenic program called etiolation.
source: However, as seeds most often germinate underneath soil, seedling development typically begins in darkness and follows a skotomorphogenic program called etiolation, characterized by rapid hypocotyl elongation and etioplast development.
evidence: This describes the typical developmental pathway studied in this work.

claim: Etiolation is characterized by rapid hypocotyl elongation and etioplast development.
source: However, as seeds most often germinate underneath soil, seedling development typically begins in darkness and follows a skotomorphogenic program called etiolation, characterized by rapid hypocotyl elongation and etioplast development.
evidence: This describes characteristics of etiolation.

claim: Light promotes seedling de-etiolation, which involves a series of morphological changes, such as cotyledon expansion, hypocotyl growth inhibition, and greening.
source: Light promotes seedling de-etiolation, which involves a series of morphological changes, such as cotyledon expansion, hypocotyl growth inhibition, and greening, that accompanies the onset of photosynthesis in chloroplasts.
evidence: This describes the de-etiolation process.

claim: During de-etiolation, etioplast–chloroplast transition is rapidly triggered by light following seedling emergence at the soil surface.
source: During de-etiolation, etioplast–chloroplast transition is thereby rapidly triggered by light following seedling emergence at the soil surface (Jarvis and López-Juez, 2013; Solymosi and Schoefs, 2010; Weier and Brown, 1970).
evidence: This describes the timing of chloroplast differentiation, supported by literature citations.

claim: A hallmark of chloroplast differentiation is the biogenesis of thylakoids, a network of internal membranes where the components of the photosynthetic electron transport chain assemble.
source: A hallmark of chloroplast differentiation is the biogenesis of thylakoids, a network of internal membranes where the components of the photosynthetic electron transport chain assemble.
evidence: This describes a key feature of chloroplast differentiation.

claim: Thylakoid biogenesis and the onset of photosynthesis rely on the concerted synthesis and coordinated assembly of chlorophylls, lipids, and proteins in both space and time.
source: Thylakoid biogenesis and the onset of photosynthesis rely on the concerted synthesis and coordinated assembly of chlorophylls, lipids, and proteins in both space and time (Jarvis and López-Juez, 2013).
evidence: This describes the complexity of thylakoid biogenesis, supported by literature citation.

claim: The thylakoids harbor the photosynthetic electron transport chain, which is composed of three complexes: photosystem II (PSII), the cytochrome b6f complex (Cyt b6f), and photosystem I (PSI).
source: The thylakoids harbor the photosynthetic electron transport chain, which is composed of three complexes: photosystem II (PSII), the cytochrome b6f complex (Cyt b6f), and photosystem I (PSI).
evidence: This describes the composition of the photosynthetic electron transport chain.

claim: Electron transfer between photosynthetic complexes is facilitated by mobile electron carriers, specifically plastoquinone and plastocyanin.
source: Electron transfer between these complexes is facilitated by mobile electron carriers, specifically the low-molecular-weight, membrane-soluble plastoquinone (electron transfer from PSII to Cyt b6f) and the lumenal protein plastocyanin (electron transfer from Cyt b6f to PSI) (Eberhard et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the electron transfer mechanism, supported by literature citation.

claim: The final reduction step catalyzed by ferredoxin-NADP(+) reductase (FNR) leads to NADPH production.
source: The final reduction step catalyzed by ferredoxin-NADP(+) reductase (FNR) leads to NADPH production.
evidence: This describes a step in the photosynthetic electron transport chain.

claim: Oxidation of water by PSII and of plastoquinone by Cyt b6f releases protons into the lumen, generating a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane that drives the activity of the thylakoid-localized chloroplast ATP synthase complex.
source: Oxidation of water by PSII and of plastoquinone by Cyt b6f releases protons into the lumen, generating a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane that drives the activity of the thylakoid-localized chloroplast ATP synthase complex.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of ATP synthesis in photosynthesis.

claim: Each of the photosynthetic complexes consists of multiple subunits encoded by the plastid or nuclear genome.
source: Each of the photosynthetic complexes consists of multiple subunits encoded by the plastid or nuclear genome (Allen et al., 2011; Jarvis and López-Juez, 2013)
evidence: This describes the genetic origin of photosynthetic complex subunits, supported by literature citations.

claim: PSII and PSI have core complexes comprising 25–30 and 15 proteins, respectively.
source: PSII and PSI have core complexes comprising 25–30 and 15 proteins, respectively (Amunts and Nelson, 2009; Caffarri et al., 2014).
evidence: This provides structural information about photosystem complexes, supported by literature citations.

claim: Cyt b6f is an eight-subunit dimeric complex.
source: Cyt b6f is an eight-subunit dimeric complex (Schöttler et al., 2015).
evidence: This provides structural information about the Cyt b6f complex, supported by literature citation.

claim: During de-etiolation, massive protein synthesis is required for assembly of the highly abundant photosynthetic complexes embedded in thylakoids.
source: During de-etiolation, massive protein synthesis is required for assembly of the highly abundant photosynthetic complexes embedded in thylakoids.
evidence: This describes a requirement for chloroplast development.

claim: The photomorphogenic program is controlled by regulation of gene expression at different levels.
source: The photomorphogenic program is controlled by regulation of gene expression at different levels (Wu, 2014).
evidence: This describes the regulatory basis of photomorphogenesis, supported by literature citation.

claim: Upon light exposure, up to one-third of Arabidopsis genes are differentially expressed, with 3/5 being upregulated and 2/5 downregulated.
source: Transcriptome analyses have revealed that upon light exposure, up to one-third of Arabidopsis genes are differentially expressed, with 3/5 being upregulated and 2/5 downregulated (Ma et al., 2001).
evidence: This provides transcriptome data from literature, supported by citation.

claim: Chloroplast proteins encoded by the nuclear genome must be imported from the cytoplasm.
source: Chloroplast proteins encoded by the nuclear genome must be imported from the cytoplasm (Jarvis and López-Juez, 2013).
evidence: This describes a requirement for chloroplast protein assembly, supported by literature citation.

claim: The general chloroplast protein import machinery is composed of the multimeric complexes TOC and TIC.
source: The general chloroplast protein import machinery is composed of the multimeric complexes Translocon at the Outer membrane of the Chloroplast (TOC) and Translocon at the Inner membrane of the Chloroplast (TIC), and selective import is based on specific recognition of transit peptide sequences by TOC receptors (Agne and Kessler, 2010; Richardson and Schnell, 2020).
evidence: This describes the chloroplast protein import machinery, supported by literature citations.

claim: Chloroplast membranes are composed mostly of glycolipids (MGDG and DGDG) and are poor in phospholipids compared to other membranes in the cell.
source: Reminiscent of their cyanobacterial origin, chloroplast membranes are composed mostly of glycolipids (mono- and di-galactosyldiacylglycerol; MGDG and DGDG) and are poor in phospholipids compared to other membranes in the cell (Bastien et al., 2016; Block et al., 1983; Kobayashi, 2016).
evidence: This describes chloroplast membrane composition, supported by literature citations.

claim: In Arabidopsis, galactolipid synthesis relies on two different pathways, defined as the eukaryotic and prokaryotic pathways depending on the organellar origin of the diacylglycerol precursor.
source: In some species, including Arabidopsis, galactolipid synthesis relies on two different pathways, defined as the eukaryotic and prokaryotic pathways depending on the organellar origin of the diacylglycerol precursor.
evidence: This describes galactolipid biosynthesis pathways in Arabidopsis.

claim: The eukaryotic pathway requires the import of diacyl-glycerol (DAG) synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) into the plastids and is referred to as the ER pathway.
source: The eukaryotic pathway requires the import of diacyl-glycerol (DAG) synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) into the plastids and is referred to as the ER pathway, whereas the prokaryotic pathway is entirely restricted to the plastid (PL) and is referred to as the PL pathway (Ohlrogge and Browse, 1995).
evidence: This describes the ER pathway for galactolipid synthesis, supported by literature citation.

claim: The prokaryotic pathway is entirely restricted to the plastid (PL) and is referred to as the PL pathway.
source: The eukaryotic pathway requires the import of diacyl-glycerol (DAG) synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) into the plastids and is referred to as the ER pathway, whereas the prokaryotic pathway is entirely restricted to the plastid (PL) and is referred to as the PL pathway (Ohlrogge and Browse, 1995).
evidence: This describes the PL pathway for galactolipid synthesis, supported by literature citation.

claim: ER pathway-derived galactolipids harbor an 18-carbon chain, whereas PL pathway–derived galactolipids harbor a 16-carbon chain at the sn2 position.
source: As signatures, ER pathway-derived galactolipids harbor an 18-carbon chain, whereas PL pathway–derived galactolipids harbor a 16-carbon chain at the sn2 position.
evidence: This describes structural signatures that distinguish galactolipids from the two pathways.

claim: Galactolipids are integral components of photosystems and thereby contribute to photochemistry and photoprotection.
source: In addition to constituting the lipid bilayer, galactolipids are integral components of photosystems and thereby contribute to photochemistry and photoprotection (Aronsson et al., 2008; Kobayashi, 2016).
evidence: This describes functional roles of galactolipids, supported by literature citations.

claim: Past studies used conventional electron microscopy to first describe the architecture of the thylakoid membrane network.
source: Past studies used conventional electron microscopy to first describe the architecture of the thylakoid membrane network.
evidence: This provides historical context for thylakoid structure studies.

claim: Based on 2D observations, researchers proposed that plant thylakoid membranes are organized as single lamellae connected to appressed multi-lamellar regions called grana.
source: Based on these 2D observations, researchers proposed that plant thylakoid membranes are organized as single lamellae connected to appressed multi-lamellar regions called grana.
evidence: This describes early models of thylakoid organization.

claim: How thylakoid lamellae are interconnected was revealed following the development of 3D electron microscopic techniques.
source: How these lamellae are interconnected was revealed only later following the development of 3D electron microscopic techniques (Staehelin and Paolillo, 2020).
evidence: This describes advances in understanding thylakoid structure, supported by literature citation.

claim: Electron tomography substantially improved comprehension of the 3D organization of the thylakoid network in chloroplasts at different developmental stages and in different photosynthetic organisms.
source: Electron tomography substantially improved our comprehension of the 3D organization of the thylakoid network in chloroplasts at different developmental stages and in different photosynthetic organisms, including Arabidopsis (Austin and Staehelin, 2011; Liang et al., 2018), Chlamydomonas (Engel et al., 2015), runner bean (Kowalewska et al., 2016), and Phaeodactylum tricornutum (Flori et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes advances in electron tomography studies, supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Electron tomography provided quantitative information on thylakoid structure such as the thylakoid layer number within the grana stack and the thickness of the stacking repeat distance of grana membrane.
source: Electron tomography also provided quantitative information on thylakoid structure such as the thylakoid layer number within the grana stack and the thickness of the stacking repeat distance of grana membrane (Daum et al., 2010; Kirchhoff et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes quantitative capabilities of electron tomography, supported by literature citations.

claim: The main drawback of electron tomography is a limit to the volume of the observation, enabling only a partial 3D reconstruction of a chloroplast.
source: Although electron tomography offers extraordinary resolution at the nanometer level, its main drawback is a limit to the volume of the observation, enabling only a partial 3D reconstruction of a chloroplast.
evidence: This describes a limitation of electron tomography.

claim: SBF-SEM allows the collection of a tomographic sequence of hundreds of images of the same area, enabling reconstruction of a much larger volume.
source: Repeated imaging and cutting allows the collection of a tomographic sequence of hundreds of images of the same area. Thereby, a much larger volume can be reconstructed in 3D to show cellular organization (Peddie and Collinson, 2014; Pinali and Kitmitto, 2014).
evidence: This describes the advantages of SBF-SEM, supported by literature citations.

claim: Biochemical fractionation of thylakoids has revealed differential lipid and protein compositions of the grana and the stroma lamellae.
source: In combination with electron microscopy, biochemical fractionation of thylakoids has revealed differential lipid and protein compositions of the grana and the stroma lamellae.
evidence: This describes findings from biochemical fractionation studies.

claim: The grana are enriched in DGDG and PSII, whereas the stroma lamellae are enriched in MGDG, Cyt b6/f, and PSI.
source: The grana are enriched in DGDG and PSII, whereas the stroma lamellae are enriched in MGDG, Cyt b6/f, and PSI (Demé et al., 2014; Koochak et al., 2019; Tomizioli et al., 2014; Wietrzynski et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes differential composition of thylakoid membrane domains, supported by literature citations.

claim: Changes in lipid and protein compositions during etioplast–chloroplast transition are tightly linked to the thylakoid architecture.
source: Changes in lipid and protein compositions during etioplast–chloroplast transition are tightly linked to the thylakoid architecture.
evidence: This describes the relationship between composition and structure during chloroplast development.

claim: Changes in MGDG to DGDG ratio are correlated with the transition from prolamellar body and prothylakoid structures (tubular membrane) to thylakoid membranes (lamellar structure).
source: In particular, changes in MGDG to DGDG ratio are correlated with the transition from prolamellar body (PLB) and prothylakoid (PT) structures (tubular membrane) to thylakoid membranes (lamellar structure) (Bottier et al., 2007; Demé et al., 2014; Mazur et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the correlation between lipid ratio and membrane structure, supported by literature citations.
